reference_title: Pavement Design for Roads, Streets, Walks, and Storage Areas

sections.title: Mix Proportioning and Control
sections.summary: Proportion/control the mix per UFC 3-250-04; design flexural strength normally uses 28-day age; consider an earlier-age design strength or high-early-strength cement if early opening is needed; fly ash gains strength slowly, so a later evaluation age may be desirable; UFC 3-201-01 sets minimum flexural strength criteria.
sections.body: Proportioning of the concrete mix and control of the concrete for pavement construction is in accordance with UFC 3-250-04. Normally, a design flexural strength at a 28-day age is used for the pavement thickness determination. When it is necessary to use the pavements at an earlier age, consideration should be given to the use of a design flexural strength at the earlier age or to the use of high early strength cement, whichever is more economical. Fly ash gains strength more slowly than cement. If used it may be desirable to select a strength value at a period other than 28 days if time permits. Refer to UFC 3-201-01 for minimum flexural strength criteria.
key_points: Default design flexural strength age: 28 days; adjust for early-opening or fly-ash mixes.
sections.applicability: Concrete mix design/proportioning for rigid pavements.

sections.title: Testing
sections.summary: Flexural strength of concrete/lean-concrete base is determined by ASTM C78/C78M.
sections.body: The flexural strength of concrete and lean concrete base is determined in accordance with ASTM C78/C78M.
key_points: Flexural strength test method: ASTM C78/C78M.
sections.applicability: Concrete flexural strength testing (also the basis for the Sc' input in the rigid design curves).

sections.title: Special Conditions
sections.summary: Adjust mix proportioning or thickness based on test results (increase section if strength is low/retrogressing, may reduce if higher than predicted); prefer adjusting the mix over changing thickness; verify state DoT specs are lump-sum-bid compatible and address ASR where local specs are used.
sections.body: Mix proportion or pavement thickness may require adjustment due to results of concrete tests. When tests results are less than predicted or a retrogression in strength, then the minimum pavement section must be increased. If the concrete strength is higher than predicted, then the thickness may be reduced. Rather than changing the thickness required as a result of tests on the concrete, the mix proportioning can be changed to increase or decrease the concrete strength, thereby not changing the thickness. If using the local state DoT specifications for the construction, verify that the specifications are compatible with lump sum bidding and that alkali-silica reaction (ASR) has adequately been addressed in your area.
key_points: Prefer adjusting the mix (strength) over changing the designed thickness when test results diverge from predictions.
sections.applicability: Quality-control response to concrete test results during construction.
